explanation: Burro is Spanish for donkey and -ito makes it small. Nobody knows for sure why; one idea is that the bulging wrap looked like the packs donkeys carried.

claims.text: The name burrito is the Spanish diminutive of burro, donkey, so it means 'little donkey'.
The names taco, tamale and quesadilla are not Spanish words for a little donkey.
Why burritos were given the name is uncertain; one suggestion is that the bulging wrap resembles the packs carried by donkeys.

evidence.restatement: Taco means a plug or wad in Mexican Spanish, tamale comes from Nahuatl tamalli and quesadilla from queso, cheese; none means little donkey.
Why the dish is called a little donkey is not known for sure; the usual suggestions liken it to the load or bedroll a donkey carries.

claimResults.note: The same call's summary says the origin of the name is less certain and gives donkey-load theories (a bedroll across a donkey's saddle, baskets carried on burros).

evidence.restatement: Spanish burro is a donkey and -ito is the diminutive ending, so burrito literally means little donkey.
